chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-‘Asemiy narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya‘qub ibn Salim from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'What do you make of the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “Thereafter women are not lawful for you”'
He said, 'Unlawful for him were only the women whom Allah had forbidden to him in this verse: “Unlawful for you to marry are your mothers, daughters…” in this verse entirely.'
'And if the matter were as they say, then he would have made lawful for you what he himself did not make lawful, because one of you would exchange [wives] whenever he wished.'
'But the matter is not as they say. The ahadith of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) are different from the ahadith of people.'

'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made lawful for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny) to marry of the women whatever he wished, except what He had forbidden to him in the Surah of Women, in this verse.'

key_terms.أَحَادِيثُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The narrations/statements of the Family of Muhammad
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ: Women are not lawful for you

ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'Thereafter women are not lawful for you' mean regarding Prophet Muhammad's marriage restrictions?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the doctrine of *Khasa'is* (special privileges) of the Prophet, asserting that his marital restrictions were unique and not subject to the general rule of polygyny applicable to other Muslims. The Imam distinguishes between the permanent prohibitions of kinship (citing Surah An-Nisa) and the temporary limit of four wives, emphasizing that the Prophet could marry as many as he willed unless specifically restricted by revelation. This supports the Shia view that the Prophet's status allowed for exceptions to standard legal rulings, reinforcing the distinctiveness of his prophetic authority.

en.sarwar: 8. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-‘Asemiy has narrated from abu al-Hassan ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya’qub ibn Salim from abu Basir who has said the following:
“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘Thereafter women are not lawful for you. . . [33:53]
He (the Imam) said, ‘Unlawful for him were the women mentioned in the verse, "Unlawful for you to marry are your mothers, daughters. . .” [4:23]
Had it been as they say it is, those who are not lawful for him became lawful for you, that one of you could exchange whenever he wanted.
It is not as they say. Ahadith of Ale Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, are different from the Ahadith of people.
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, made it lawful for His Holy prophet to marry as many as he wanted of women except those unlawful in this verse [4:23].’”
